Exact differential base (a B_2 sequence) constructed as follows: Start with a(0)=0. For n>=1, let S be the set of all differences a(j)-a(i) for 0 <= i < j <= n-1, and let d be the smallest positive integer not in S. If, for every i in 1..n-1, a(n-1) + d - a(i) is not in S, then a(n) = a(n-1) + d. Otherwise, let r be the smallest positive integer such that, for every i in 1..n-1, neither a(n-1) + r - a(i) nor a(n-1) + r + d - a(i) is in S; then a(n) = a(n-1) + r and a(n+1) = a(n) + d.

The members of B(n) are paths of weight n that start at (0,0), end on but never go below the horizontal axis, and whose steps are of the following four kinds: an (1,0)-step with weight 1, an (1,0)-step with weight 2, a (1,1)-step with weight 2, and a (1,-1)-step with weight 1. Read one digit d at the time, starting from the first one; extend S with the smallest multiple of d not yet present in the sequence. Zeros are not read.
Similar to A100787, but alternate with addition and multiplication instead. See Comments section for more information.
Irregular triangle read by rows T(n,k) in which row n lists n blocks, where the m-th block consists of the divisors of j multiplied by A000041(m-1), where j = n - m + 1 and 1 <= m <= n.
Irregular triangle read by rows T(n,k) in which row n lists n blocks, where the block m consists of the divisors of m multiplied by A000041(n-m), with 1 <= m <= n.
Square array, read by ascending antidiagonals, where row n gives all solutions n > 0 to A000120(n+1) = A000120((n+1)*k), A000120 is the Hamming weight.
The number of overpartitions of n having more non-overlined parts than overlined parts.
a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) = a(n-1) - min(a(n-1),n) if nonnegative and not already in the sequence, otherwise a(n) = a(n-1) + min(a(n-1),n).
a(n) is the number of distinct resistances that can be produced using at most n unit resistors in a planar network.

a(n) = denominator(p(n, x)) / (n!*denominator(bernoulli(n, x))), where p(n, x) = Sum_{k=0..n} E2(n, k)*binomial(x + k, 2*n) / Product_{j=1..n} (j - x) and E2(n, k) are the second-order Eulerian numbers A201637.
Number of length-n binary mesosome-avoiding strings.
Number of distinct resistances that can be produced using at most n unit resistors in series, parallel, bridge or fork configurations.

Nodes read by depth in a binary tree defined as: Root = 1; an even node N has a left child N + 1 if N + 1 is not a prime, and an odd node N has a left child sqrt(N + 2) if sqrt(N + 2) is a prime; the right child of a node N is 2*N.

If a(n) is odd, add to a(n) its odd digits and iterate; if a(n) is even, add to a(n) its even digits and iterate; if an iteration reproduces a term already in the sequence, don't do this iteration and extend the sequence with the smallest integer not yet present in the sequence.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct terms > 0 such that the n-th digit of the sequence is present in the absolute difference |a(n) - a(n+1)|.
Length of the longest 2-increasing sequence of positive integer triples with entries <= n.
a(0)=0. For n > 0, a(n+1) = 2*a(n) if the sum of digits of 2*a(n) exceeds that of a(n); otherwise, a(n+1) is the smallest unused nonnegative integer.
Numbers k such that the arithmetic derivative of k is a multiple of phi(k).

Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive numbers such that for any n > 0, a(n+1) can be obtained by replacing in the decimal representation of a(n) some nonempty substring m (without leading zero) by a divisor of m or by a positive multiple of m.
Decimal numbers m such that the product of the binary string of m and the binary string of m in reverse contains the binary string of m as a substring.
Number with a record number of divisors whose prime factorizations contain no repeated exponents.
Number of distinct sets { p(i) - p(j) : 1 <= i <= j <= n } where p ranges over all permutations of [n].
Irregular triangle T(n, k), n > 0, k = 1..A343650(n), read by rows; the n-th row lists the divisors d of n such that the product d * (n/d) can be computed without carries in binary.
Optimal lower bounds for the permanent of 312-pattern avoiding 0-1 matrices.
Shortest distance from curve start to end along the segments of dragon curve expansion level n, and which is the diameter of the curve as a graph.
Flattened tetrangle of reversed strict integer partitions, sorted first by length and then colexicographically.

For any number n with binary expansion Sum_{k = 1..m} 2^e_k (where 0 <= e_1 < ... < e_m), a(n) = Product_{k = 1..m} prime(1+A002262(e_k))^2^A025581(e_k) (where prime(k) denotes the k-th prime number).
Number of integer partitions of 2*n with reverse-alternating sum >= 0.
Triangle read by rows where T(n,k) is the number of integer partitions of n with reverse-alternating sum k ranging from -n to n in steps of 2.
Number of compositions of n with no adjacent triples (..., x, y, z, ...) where x < y < z or x > y > z.
a(n) is the lowest nonnegative exponent k such that n!^k is the product of the divisors of n!.
Number of integer partitions of 2n with reverse-alternating sum -2.
T(n, k) = (3^(-k)*n!*2^(n - 3*k))/(k!*(n - 3*k)!), for n >= 0 and 0 <= k <= floor(n/3). Triangle read by rows.

a(n) = Sum_{i=1..n} nac(i,n) where nac(i,n) is the n-th i-bonacci number. The n-th i-bonacci number here is equal to 1 for the first i terms, with subsequent terms equaling the sum of the previous n terms.
Numbers k that require fewer than k steps to reach 1 under the 3x+1 map.
Least k >= 1 such that sigma(k)/tau(k) has denominator n or zero if no k exists.
Irregular triangle T(n, k), n > 0, k = 1..A091220(n), read by rows; the n-th row gives, in ascending order, the distinct integers k such that A048720(k, m) = n for some m.
Decimal expansion of Sum_{n>=0} A346838(n) / n!.
Number of Motzkin paths of length n avoiding UHHD.
Numbers whose number of odd divisors is not equal to 2.
Irregular triangle whose n-th row lists the integers m such that the n-th necklace polynomial is divisible by the m-th cyclotomic polynomial.
Irregular triangle whose n-th row lists the integers m such that the n-th necklace polynomial is divisible by x^m-1.
Indices of first occurrences of n in A347409.
Number of factorizations of n with reverse-alternating product > 1.
Number of compositions (ordered partitions) of n into at most 4 prime powers (including 1).
Number of compositions (ordered partitions) of n into at most 5 prime powers (including 1).
Number of compositions (ordered partitions) of n into at most 6 prime powers (including 1).
Palindromes setting a new record of their number of prime divisors A001222.
Irregular triangle T(n, k), n > 0, k = 1..A067399(n), read by rows; the n-th row gives, in ascending order, the distinct integers k such that A067138(k, m) = n for some m.
Index of first occurrence of n in A307730.
Irregular table T(n, k), n > 0, k = 1..A000120(n), read by rows; the n-th contains, in ascending order, the distinct powers of 2 summing to n.
a(0) = A002858(1) = 1, followed by the greatest Ulam numbers A002858 to form a complete sequence (see algorithm below).
Numbers with record values of the denominator of the harmonic mean of their divisors.
a(1) = 1; a(n+1) = 2*a(n) if the digit sum of a(n) is already in the sequence, otherwise a(n+1) = digitsum(a(n)).
Length of the shortest string over the alphabet {1,...,n} such that every subset of {1,...,n} appears as a substring (in some order).
Numbers with record values of the denominator of the harmonic mean of their unitary divisors.
Numbers k where the ratios A099378(k)/k reach a record value.
Number of weakly alternating compositions of n.
Number of integer partitions of n with at least one part of odd multiplicity that is not the first or last.
Numbers k such that there exists m, 1 <= m <= k with the property that A000178(k) / m! is a square, where A000178(k) = k$ = 1!*2!*...*k! is the superfactorial of k.
Number of ternary triples (u,v,w) with 1 <= u < v < w <= n.
Products of three consecutive terms of A349227: a(n) = A349227(n) * A349227(n+1) * A349227(n+2).
Numbers k >= 1 such that A018804(k) divided by A000010(k) is an integer.
Number of ways to write n as w^4 + x^2 + y^2 + z^2 with x - y a power of two (including 2^0 = 1).
Given the sequence of the digits of the Champernowne constant A033307 we start with number 1 and advance as many digits as the number that it indicates. If the digit is 0 then advance 10 positions.
a(1)=1; for n > 1, a(n) = a(n-1) + (sum of odd-indexed digits of a(n-1)) - (sum of even-indexed digits of a(n-1)).
a(n) is the constant term in expansion of Product_{k=1..n} (x^(k^2) + 1/x^(k^2))^2.
Indices of odd terms in A350877.
a(1)=1. For n>1, a(n)=A095848(n) divided by the smallest number in A095848 that is divisible by the largest prime divisor of A095848(n).
Four-column table read by rows giving quadruples of integers [w,x,y,z] with w > 0, x > 1, y > 1 and z > 0 such that y^2 - y - x*z = 0 and x^2 = w*y, sorted by y then by x.
Numbers k where 3k sets a record for the number of divisors of multiples of 3.
Number of subsets of {1,2,...,n} such that no two elements differ by 3 or 4.
Irregular triangle read by rows: the n-th row contains the values 0..2^n-1 sorted first by Hamming weight and then by position in reflected Gray code.
Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the (n-th)-to-last digit of 2^p such that p == k + A123384(n-1) (mod A005054(n)); k >= 0.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that the first digit of |a(n) - a(n+1)| is the n-th digit of the sequence (integers including a zero are excluded).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that the last digit of |a(n) - a(n+1)| is the n-th digit of the sequence.

a(1) = 1; a(2) = 2; for n > 2, a(n) is the smallest positive number that has not appeared that shares a factor with a(n-1) and whose binary expansion has no 1-bit in common with the binary expansion of a(n-1).
The binary expansion of a(n) encodes the runs of consecutive 1's in the binary expansion of n (see Comments section for precise definition).
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that for any n and k coprime the binary expansions of a(n) and a(k) have no common 1's.
Jackpot integers: number of steps needed by n to win a "jackpot" (see the explanation below in the Comments and Example sections) or -1 if this will never occur.
Irregular triangle read by rows; T(n,k) = 2^k (mod prime(n)), terminating when T(n,k) = 1.
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order is empty, a singleton, or has its own run-lengths as a subsequence (not necessarily consecutive) that is already counted.
Numbers k such that the k-th composition in standard order (A066099) is empty, a singleton, or has run-lengths that are a consecutive subsequence that is already counted.

a(0)=0, a(1)=1; thereafter a(n) = smallest nonnegative integer not among the earlier terms of the sequence such that a(n) and a(n-2) have no common 1-bits in their binary representations and also a(n) and a(n-1) have no common 1-bits in their binary representations.
Numbers k such that k divides A353790(k), where A353790(n) = phi(A003973(n)) * A064989(A003973(n)).
Numbers that are neither an odd prime power nor twice an odd prime power.

a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1, a(2) = 2; for k >= 2, given a(k), the sequence is extended by adjoining two terms: a(2*k-1) = smallest m >= 0 not among a(0) .. a(k) such that {m, a(k), a(k+1), ..., a(2*k-2)} are pairwise disjoint in binary, and a(2*k) = smallest m >= 0 not among a(0) .. a(k) such that {m, a(k), ..., a(2*k-1)} are pairwise disjoint in binary.
Numbers k for which phi(A267099(k)) is equal to phi(k), where A267099 is fully multiplicative involution swapping the positions of 4k+1 and 4k+3 primes, and phi is Euler totient function.
Number of ways to tile a double-hexagon strip of n hexagons, using single and double hexagons.

Rectangular array read by antidiagonals. T(m,n) is the number of degree n monic polynomials in GF_2[x] such that each irreducible factor in the prime factorization has multiplicity no greater than m, m>=1, n>=0.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive number that has not yet appeared that shares a factor with a(n-1) and the difference | a(n) - a(n-1) | is distinct from all previous differences.
a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) is the smallest positive number that has not yet appeared that shares a factor with a(n-1) and the difference a(n) - a(n-1) is distinct from all previous differences.
Numbers whose skew binary representation (A169683) is palindromic.
Positions of odd terms in A344005.
a(0)=0; for n > 0, a(n) = 2*a(n-1) if n-1 is prime, a(n-1) + 1 otherwise.
Factorial splitting: write n! = x*y*z with x <= y <= z and minimal z-x; sequence gives value of x.

Irregular triangle T(n, k), n > 0, k = 1..A093640(n), read by rows; the n-th row contains in ascending order the divisors of n whose binary expansions appear as substrings in the binary expansion of n.
a(n) is the smallest number that has exactly n odious divisors (A000069).
Positions of records in A227872, i.e., integers whose number of odious divisors sets a new record.
Numbers whose prime indices are all odd and cover an initial interval of odd positive integers.
Inventory of positions as an irregular table; row 0 contains 0, subsequent rows contain the 0-based positions of 0's, followed by the position of 1's, of 2's, etc. in prior rows flattened.
Array read by descending antidiagonals: T(n,k) is the number of cycles of the permutation given by the order of elimination in the Josephus problem for n numbers and a count of k; n, k >= 1.
Numbers m such that A357761(m) > A357761(k) for all k < m.

Given a row of n payphones (or phone booths), all initially unused, how many ways are there for n people to choose the payphones, assuming each always chooses one of the most distant payphones from those in use already? We consider here only the distance to the closest neighbor (in contrast to A095236).
Numbers k such that sigma(2*k) > 2*k*sqrt(gamma(2*k)), where sigma(k) = A000203(k) is the sum of the divisors of k and gamma(k) = A007947(k) is the greatest squarefree divisor of k.
Number of transitive ordered rooted trees with n nodes.
a(n) is the smallest number k with exactly n divisors that can be written in the form m + digsum(m), for some m (A176995).
a(n) is the smallest number whose divisors include exactly n that can be written in the form m + reverse(m), for some m (A067030).
Starting from 1, successively take the smallest "Choix de Bruxelles" (A323286) which is not already in the sequence.
Number of multiset partitions of integer partitions of n with all distinct block sizes.
Number of Wachs permutations of size n.
Irregular table read by rows; the n-th row lists the divisors d of 2*n such that the binary expansions of d and 2*n have no common 1-bit.
a(n) is the number of free polyiamonds of n cells with chessboard coloring.
a(n) is the smallest tetranacci number (A000078) with exactly n prime factors (counted with multiplicity).
Irregular triangle read row by row. The k-th row are integers from 0 to 2^k-1 in base 2 ordered in graded reverse lexicographical order.
Total number of edges after n generations in hexagonal graph constructed in first quadrant (see Comments in A360501 for precise definition).
Numerators of breadth-first numerator-denominator-incrementing enumeration of rationals in (0,1).
Numbers k where A093653(k)/A000120(k) sets a new record.
a(n) is the least number k such that A093653(k)/A000120(k) = n.
a(n) is the smallest positive number not among the terms between a(n-1) and the previous most recent occurrence of a(n-1) inclusive; if a(n-1) is a first occurrence, set a(n)=1; a(1)=1.

Lexicographically earliest sequence of positive integers such that the sums SumXOR_{i = 1+k*2^e..(k+1)*2^e} a(i) with k, e >= 0 are all distinct (where SumXOR is the analog of summation under the binary XOR operation).

For any number k >= 0, let T_k be the triangle whose base corresponds to the ternary expansion of k (without leading zeros) and other values, say t above u and v, satisfy t = (-u-v) mod 3; this sequence lists the numbers k such that T_k has 3-fold rotational symmetry.
Numbers k with record values of the ratio A000005(k)/A246600(k) between the total number of divisors of k and the number of divisors d of k such that the bitwise OR of k and d is equal to k.
Number of 2-balanced binary words of length n with respect to the permutations of the symbols.
Maximum number of ways in which a set of integer-sided squares can tile an n X 3 rectangle, up to rotations and reflections.
Sequence that alternately doubles and squares the previous number; a(0) = 1.
Positive integers k such that the largest power of p dividing k is larger than or equal to the largest power of q dividing k (i.e., A305720(k,p) >= A305720(k,q)) for all primes p and q with p < q.
a(n) = Sum_{k=0..n} n^notdivides(k, n), where notdivides(k, n) = 0 if k divides n, otherwise 1.
Numbers k such that 3^k + 2*k is prime.
a(n) is the least positive number with distinct decimal digits and n prime factors, counted with multiplicity, or -1 if there is no such number.
Numbers k such that A243071(k) < k.

For p = 5 and n > 0, write n = p^m + k, m >= 0, with maximal p^m <= n, with 0 <= k < p^(m+1) - p^m, then for n such that k=0, a(n)=n, and for n such that k > 0, a(n) is the smallest q*a(k), prime q != p, that is not already a term.

For p = 7 and n > 0, write n = p^m + k, m >= 0, with maximal p^m <= n, with 0 <= k < p^(m+1) - p^m, then for n such that k=0, a(n)=n, and for n such that k > 0, a(n) is the smallest q*a(k), prime q != p, that is not already a term.
The smallest number k that has exactly n of its divisors in A005153.
Number of ways to write n as a nonnegative linear combination of a strict integer partition.
Number of (3+)-free binary strings of length n.

Table read by antidiagonals upward: T(n,k) is the number of binary strings of length k with the property that every substring of length A070939(n) is lexicographically earlier than the binary expansion of n; n, k >= 0.
Number of non-subset-sums of strict integer partitions of n.

Square array A(n, k), n, k >= 0, read and filled by upwards antidiagonals the greedy way with distinct nonnegative integers such that the binary expansions of any two distinct terms in the same row or column or antidiagonal have no common 1's.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that for n>1, Sum_{i=1..n, a(i)<=n} a(a(i)) is prime.
Number of unlabeled graphs on n vertices without 4-cycles or 5-cycles.

Square array A(n, k), n, k >= 0, read and filled by upwards antidiagonals the greedy way with distinct nonnegative integers such that the binary expansions of any two distinct terms in the same row or column have no common 1's.
a(n) = the maximum number of distinct tilings of a polyiamond of size n using any combination of polyiamond tiles of sizes 1 through n.
Number of subsets of {1..n} whose cardinality cannot be written as a nonnegative linear combination of the elements.
Minimum size of a set of polyominoes with n-1 cells such that all free polyominoes with n cells can be obtained by adding one cell to one of the polyominoes in the set.
G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = 1 / (1 - x * (1 + x + x^2) * A(x^3)).
G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = 1 / (1 - x * (1 + x + x^2 + x^3) * A(x^4)).
G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = 1 / (1 - x * (1 + x + x^2 + x^3 + x^4) * A(x^5)).
G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = 1 / (1 - x - x * A(x^3)).
G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = 1 / (1 - x - x * A(x^4)).
G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = 1 / (1 - x - x * A(x^5)).

a(1,2) = 1,2. let i,j represent a(n-2), a(n-1) respectively and let M(i) = {i,j}. For n > 2, if one of i,j is prime (p), and the other (m) is not, then if p!|m, a(n) is the least novel multiple of p. If p|m, a(n) = p*m. If both terms in M are nonprime a(n) is the least novel multiple of the smallest prime which does not divide i*j.
Degrees of number fields unramified away from 2.
Number of non-isomorphic set-systems of weight n satisfying a strict version of the axiom of choice.
Square array read by ascending antidiagonals: T(n,k) = Sum_{i=ceiling((k-n)/2)..floor((k+n-1)/2)} binomial(k,i), with n >= 1, k >= 0.

Irregular table T(n, k), n > 0, k = 1..A368195(n), read by rows: the n-th row lists the numbers that can be obtained by replacing any positive number without leading zeros, say m, appearing in the decimal expansion of n by one of the divisors of m.

Irregular table T(n, k), n > 0, k = 1..A368314(n), read by rows: the n-th row lists the numbers that can be obtained by replacing any positive number without leading zeros, say m, appearing in the binary expansion of n by one of the divisors of m.
Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k) is the position of k within the Christmas tree pattern (A367562) of order n, with n >= 1 and k >= 0.
Number of binary words of length n not containing the substrings 0000, 0001, 0011, 0111.
a(n) is the number of unlabeled planar modular lattices on n nodes.
Decimal expansion of the probability that the T tetromino appears when the 4th cell is added in diffusion-limited aggregation on the square lattice.
a(n) = sum of the origin-to-boundary graph-distances of all partitions of n.
Numbers with a record high excess of even over odd divisors; so indices of record lows in A048272.
a(n) is the constant term in expansion of Product_{k=1..n} (x^(2*k-1) + 1/x^(2*k-1))^2.
Irregular triangle read by rows: row n lists the values of the vertices at the n-th level of the MI graph (see comments).
Expansion of g.f. A(x) satisfying Sum_{n>=0} (-1)^n * x^n * Product_{k=0..n} (x^(2*k+1) + A(x)) = theta_3(x).
Number of pairs (p,q) of partitions of n such that the set of parts in q is a subset of the set of parts in p.
Volumes of integer-sided cuboids in which either the surface area divides the volume or vice versa (assuming dimensionless unit of length).

a(1) = 1; a(2) = 2; for n > 2, a(n) is smallest unused number such that a(n) shares a factor with a(n-1) and sopfr(a(n)) shares a factor with sopfr(a(n-1)), where sopfr(k) is the sum of the primes dividing k, with repetition.
a(0) = 1, a(n) = result of eliminating the digit 7 from the sum of all previous terms for n>=1.
Expansion of g.f. A(x) satisfying Sum_{n>=0} Product_{k=1..n} (x^(2*k-1) - 3*A(x)) = 1 - 2*Sum_{n>=1} x^(n^2).
Numbers k such that (9^k + 9*k)/9 is prime.
a(0)=1; a(n) = sum of all previous terms, eliminating repeated digits (starting from the left).
Numbers whose binary indices are connected, where two numbers are connected iff they have a common factor.
Numbers whose binary indices are connected and pairwise indivisible, where two numbers are connected iff they have a common factor. A hybrid ranking sequence for connected antichains of multisets.
Number of achiral polyominoes composed of n tetrahedral cells of the hyperbolic regular tiling with Schläfli symbol {3,3,oo}.

Irregular triangle read by rows: n-th row gives congruence classes s such that the n-th prime q is a quadratic residue modulo an odd prime p if and only if p = plus or minus s for some s (mod m), where m = q if q is of the form 4k + 1, else m = 4q.
Table(n,k) of binary strings of length n which have the same number of k long 0...00 and 0...01 substrings, where n>=0 and k>=2, read by downwards antidiagonals.
Number of Dyck paths of semilength n such that neighboring peaks differ in height by at most one and first and last peak are at height one.
Numbers n such that each binary index k (from row n of A048793) has the same sum of binary indices A029931(k).
Number of biquanimous subsets of {1..n}. Sets with a subset having the same sum as the complement.
Decimal expansion of Integral_{x=0..oo} 1 / (1 + x^7) dx.
Smallest number reachable starting from 1 and taking n steps either doubling or doubling+reversing.
Largest number reachable starting from 1 and taking n steps either doubling or doubling+reversing.
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct nonnegative integers such that for any n >= 0, the binary expansions of a(n), a(2*n+1) and a(2*n+2) have distinct 1's.
Least k such that the rank of the elliptic curve y^2 = x^3 - k^2*x + 1 is n, or -1 if no such k exists.
A positive integer 2^k*m, where m is odd and k >= 0, belongs to this sequence iff the Jacobi symbol (F_n/m) = -1 for only a finite number of Fermat numbers F_n = A000215(n).
New record minima in A071961, divided by 2 and negated.
Numbers k that divide the k-th tangent (or "zag") number.
a(n) is the number of binary strings of length n not containing the substrings 0000, 0001, 0011, 0111, 1111.
Numbers k for which A003415(k) is a multiple of A276085(k), where A003415 is the arithmetic derivative and A276085 is the primorial base log-function.
Number of (binary) heaps where n is the sum of their length and the size of the element set [k].
Lexicographically earliest sequence of distinct positive integers such that for A(k) <= n < A(k+1); rad(Product_{i = 1..n} a(i)) = A002110(k), where A = A002110, rad = A007947, k >= 0, n >= 1.
a(n) is the numerator of x(n) = (2*x(n-1) + c(n)) mod 1, where c(n) = 1/n if n is a power of 3 and 0 otherwise, with x(0) = 0.
Number of integer compositions of n whose leaders of anti-runs are weakly decreasing.
Number of integer compositions of n whose leaders of strictly increasing runs are weakly decreasing.
a(n) = a(n-1) + rotate(a(n-1), n-2 digits right) with a(1) = 1.
a(n) = a(n-1) + rotate(a(n-1), n-1 digits right) with a(1) = 1.
a(n) = a(n-1) + rotate(a(n-1), n-2 digits left) with a(1) = 1.
a(n) = a(n-1) + rotate(a(n-1), n-1 digits left) with a(1) = 1.
Number of integer compositions of n whose leaders of weakly decreasing runs are distinct.

Irregular triangle read by rows: T(n,k), n >= 0, k >= 1, in which if n is even then row n lists the first A008619(n) even indexed terms of A027336 otherwise if n is odd then row n lists the first A008619(n) odd indexed terms of A027336.
Numbers whose Collatz trajectory is a Sidon sequence.
The number of infinitary divisors of n!.
Number of subsets of {1,2,...,n} such that no two elements differ by 3 or 5.
Number of subsets of {1,2,...,n} such that no two elements differ by 4 or 5.
Number of subsets of {1,2,...,n} such that no two elements differ by 3, 4, or 5.
Orders k of groups G such that Inn(G) is isomorphic to Z(Aut(G)) for at least one G of order k.
Irregular triangle where row n lists m such that rad(m) | n and bigomega(m) <= bigomega(n), where rad = A007947 and bigomega = A001222.

Run-sums of the sequence of first differences of prime-powers.
